submission.justification: Radiator-R3 at 6 cm thickness is recommended based on the following analysis: (1) R2 is eliminated due to 40% transparency loss, far exceeding the 10% threshold. (2) Both R1 (3% loss) and R3 (6% loss) pass the ageing requirement. (3) R3 at maximum thickness (6 cm) was selected based on physics reasoning that greater radiator thickness generally provides better separation power. CRITICAL LIMITATION: The simulation tool was unavailable, so the 3.5 sigma pion/kaon separation requirement at 10 GeV/c could not be verified. This recommendation should be validated with simulation data before final implementation. The choice of maximum thickness (6 cm) aims to maximize photon yield and separation power within the allowed range.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: Simulation tool was unavailable. No separation performance data obtained. R3 at 6 cm selected based on physics reasoning that maximum thickness should provide maximum photon yield.

requirements.requirement: Pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c must be at least 3.5 sigma (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: Could not be verified due to simulation tool unavailability. No simulation data available to confirm this critical requirement is met.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year ageing must not exceed 10% (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: R3 shows 6% transparency loss in ageing test, well below the 10% threshold. R1 (3%) and R3 (6%) passed; R2 (40%) failed.
Recommended thickness of 6 cm is at the upper limit of the allowed range (1-6 cm).

requirements.requirement: Radiator must be one of three candidates
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 is one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
